identity.title: EP Aquarii: A New Picture of the Circumstellar Envelope

paper_type_evidence.quote: New analyses of earlier ALMA observations of oxygen-rich AGB star EP Aquarii are presented, which complete a previously published analysis and offer a different interpretation of the morpho-kinematics of the circumstellar envelope (CSE).

We use archival ALMA observations of the CO(2-1) and SiO(5-4) line emissions of EP Aquarii that were performed in 2016 and 2019 under projects ADS/JAO.ALMA#2016.1.00057.S and ADS/JAO.ALMA#2018.1.00750.S, respectively (PI W. Homan).

evidence.quote: located at 119 ± 6 pc from the solar system (van Leeuwen 2007; Gaia Collaboration 2018)

question.value: Re-evaluate the morpho-kinematics of the circumstellar envelope of EP Aquarii—specifically the origin of the high-velocity wings, the formation and spiral nature of the equatorial density enhancement, the bipolar outflows, and the western depression in SiO(5-4) emission—using new analyses of archival ALMA CO(2-1) and SiO(5-4) data.

evidence.quote: The aim of the present article is therefore to shed new light on these issues, by presenting new additional analyses of the emissions of the CO(2-1) and SiO(5-4) lines, in particular in the close neighbourhood of the star.

analysis_steps.goal: Separate and quantify the two components of the high Doppler velocity wings

method.value: Integrate TM0 SiO(5-4) spectra in 20 mas wide annular rings from mean radius 10 mas to 390 mas; measure the full width at 10% of maximum (FWTM) as a function of R; extrapolate the red-shifted spectrum edge down to continuum level in the combined data to measure V_max as a function of R and omega; construct |Vz| vs R PV maps and intensity maps in 8 < |Vz| < 12 km s^-1 and 12 < |Vz| < 20 km s^-1.

evidence.quote: we use the high resolution TM0 data in the form of Doppler velocity spectra of SiO(5-4) emission, integrated in 20 mas broad annular rings centred on the star with mean radii increasing from 10 mas to 390 mas in steps of 20 mas. claims.hypothesis: The high Doppler velocity wings reaching ~±20 km s^-1 in EP Aqr are produced by two narrow polar jets building up between ~20 and ~100 au as previously proposed by Tuan-Anh et al. (2019), rather than by pulsation and convective-cell shocks close to the star.
claims.experiment: Measure the full width at 10% maximum (FWTM) of SiO(5-4) spectra in 20 mas annular rings from 10 to 390 mas using high-resolution TM0 data, extrapolate the bulk CSE maximum velocity V_max in the combined data, and inspect |Vz| vs R PV diagrams and velocity-slice maps.
claims.result: FWTM follows 21.3 + 19.0 exp(-R/0.10) km s^-1, showing that velocities up to ±20 km s^-1 are confined within R < 200 mas, while the bulk polar outflow reaches a maximal velocity of ~12 km s^-1 at larger radii.
claims.finding: The high-velocity wings consist of two distinct components—the upper velocity end of the polar outflows (~12 km s^-1) and inner shock-induced line broadening within 200 mas (~20 km s^-1); the earlier jet interpretation mixed these two components and is refuted.

evidence.quote: This analysis gives therefore evidence for two major contributions to the high velocity wings of the SiO(5-4) Doppler velocity spectrum: one, extending up to some 12 km s − 1, is simply the upper edge of the velocity distribution of the polar outflows; the other, reaching up to 20 km s − 1, is confined to the close neighbourhood of the star
The interpretation given by Tuan-Anh et al. (2019) of these high velocity wings, using data of lower angular resolution, was mixing both contributions.

claims.hypothesis: The EDE in EP Aqr is formed by gravitational focusing from a white dwarf companion orbiting at R ~ 400 mas, which creates a single grand-design spiral in CO(2-1) emission (Homan et al. 2018, 2020a).
claims.experiment: Examine CO(2-1) Vz vs omega maps in 100 mas wide rings down to R = 100 mas using TM0 and combined data, and average the four central velocity channels (-0.75 < Vz < 0.53 km s^-1) to correct for the ~10 deg tilt of the EDE plane.
claims.result: The EDE is already present at 100 < R < 200 mas with rotation at a few km s^-1 scale (well inside the proposed 400 mas companion orbit), and when the 10 deg tilt is averaged over the four central channels, the single spiral pattern disappears into overlapping eccentric circular arcs.
claims.finding: The birth of the EDE occurs very close to the star (R < 200 mas) and the identification of a single companion-induced spiral is not robust once the EDE tilt is accounted for.

claims.hypothesis: The western blue-shifted depression in SiO(5-4) emission around R ~ 400 mas is caused by UV molecular photodissociation from a white dwarf companion located at 0.4 arcsec west of the star (Homan et al. 2020a), versus being the wake of an episodic mass ejection.
claims.experiment: Construct Vz vs omega maps in 100 mas rings and Vz vs R PV maps integrated over the western void sector (240 deg < omega < 300 deg) and northern void sector (280 deg < omega < 360 deg) for both SiO(5-4) and CO(2-1).
claims.result: Both the western blue-shifted void (peak-to-valley ~6) and a similar northern red-shifted void (peak-to-valley ~3) lie directly in the wake of faster expanding shells (R ~ 0.5-1 arcsec, V ~ 5-10 km s^-1) seen in SiO and CO, with an earlier shell visible in CO a few decades prior, and SiO emission has resumed at R < 200 mas.
claims.finding: The western SiO(5-4) depression is unsupported as a white dwarf UV dissociation zone (which would also irradiate the red hemisphere) and is instead explained as a density void in the wake of a standard episodic mass ejection triggered by pulsation and convective cells.

claims.hypothesis: The latitudinal dependence of the radial expansion velocity between the EDE and the polar outflows follows V = V_eq + (V_pole - V_eq) sin^2(alpha) as assumed in Hoai et al. (2019).
claims.experiment: Compare the observed CO(2-1) emission ridges in Vz vs R position-velocity diagrams within narrow position angle wedges against theoretical curves f(alpha) = sin^n(alpha) for n = 1/2, 1, and 2.
claims.result: The observed PV ridges at low stellar latitudes follow curves with n < 1 rather than n = 2.
claims.finding: The radial expansion velocity drops rapidly only at small stellar latitudes where the outflow interacts with the dense EDE, corresponding to sin^n(alpha) with n < 1 and refuting the n = 2 assumption.

evidence.quote: Comparison with low latitude observations, as shown in the right panels of Figure 11 (see also Figure S3), favours clearly values of n smaller than 1, in contradiction with the arbitrary assumption made in Hoai et al. (2019).

limitations_admitted.value: Below R ~ 200 mas, available data cannot disentangle the simultaneous contributions of expansion, rotation, EDE formation, dust condensation, and pulsation/convective shock waves.

evidence.quote: Unfortunately, with presently available data, it is difficult to tell apart, in the immediate neighbourhood of the star, say below R∼ 200 mas, the contributions of expansion, of rotation and of phenomena related to the generation of the nascent wind: dust formation and shock waves caused by the interaction between stellar pulsation and convective cell partition (see Section 5).

limitations_admitted.value: The nearly face-on inclination (~10 deg) of the EDE prevents a precise evaluation of its radial expansion velocity.

limitations_admitted.value: Angular resolution is insufficient to resolve the fine spatial/temporal structure associated with the ~110-day stellar pulsation period, and lack of reliable light curve measurements prevents relating inner shock features to stellar phase.

limitations_admitted.value: The physical mechanism governing the precocious formation of the equatorial disc (and why CO emission has not resumed at R < 200 mas after the western mass ejection while SiO has) remains unexplained, preventing a definitive claim of model uniqueness.

referee_caveats_inferred: No radiative transfer or hydrodynamical modelling is performed; interpretations of optical depth, excitation temperature effects (beyond a simple Boltzmann factor estimate), and shock wakes are purely kinematic and geometric.
